text:
maria.gomez: Quick sync — we had two customers this morning hit odd behavior where requests were routed to a cheaper variant after regional capacity flaps and the console trace just shows a generic "route fallback" line. We need to decide a) which routing headers to emit, b) what to show in the trace UI, and c) sampling rules so we actually capture useful playback.

zach.lee: Can you paste an example header trace you saw?

maria.gomez: Yep — scrubbed example from staging:
```
X-Rd-Route: tier=premium;region=eu-west;policy=latency-first;decision=choose_v1
X-Rd-Decision-Id: d_2f9c1a
X-Rd-Fallback: tried=v1-8q->v1-4q;reason=quota;fallback-step=1
X-Rd-Sampled: true
```
The issue: dashboard groups it as "fallback" with no context — customer support then sees only "fallback occurred" and asks engineering.

cheng.wu: Two problems: (1) telemetry cardiniality if we emit full tenant/model tags on every request, (2) trace sampling — we only store traces for 0.5% of requests now. Might miss the interesting ones.

priya.sundar: Proposal: emit lightweight routing headers (tier, region, decision_id, fallback_chain) and always force-sample traces when fallback_chain != "". For dashboards, show a tiny breadcrumb timeline per request: "policy eval -> chosen variant -> fallback -> final variant" with reasons. :sparkles:

zach.lee: I like forced sampling on fallback. Also add metrics: route_evaluations_total, fallback_count{tier,region,model_variant}, and fallback_latency_penalty_seconds_bucket. That lets us build per-route SLO dashboards.

maria.gomez: Agreed. Also let's not include clear tenant ids in public dashboards. Hash tenant id for dashboards and keep raw tenant only in secure logs.

cheng.wu: Hashing is fine. For metrics, we can use a low-cardinality tag for dashboards (tier, region, hashed_tenant_prefix) and attach high-cardinality metadata only to sampled traces. That avoids series explosion.

priya.sundar: UX item: in request trace viewer add a "routing decision" panel with a small timeline and a button "simulate against different policy" which calls an internal simulate endpoint. Example API:
```
POST /internal/routing/simulate
Body: {"decision_id":"d_2f9c1a","simulate_policy":"cost-first"}
```
It returns what the decision would have been and why. That helps support repros.

zach.lee: Implementation note: the simulate endpoint must be idempotent and able to replay policy eval without hitting quotas/capacity. Do it against a read-only snapshot of state (quotas, region capacity).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/route-telemetry -> staging (ci #4321) :rocket:

maria.gomez: Good. For the headers, let's standardize names. Proposed header spec in config repo:
```
X-Rd-Route: tier=<tier>;region=<region>;policy=<policy>
X-Rd-Decision-Id: <id>
X-Rd-Fallback-Chain: tried=<v1-8q>,<v1-4q>;reason=quota
X-Rd-Sampled: true|false
```
Keep them short and parseable.

cheng.wu: Agree on the shape, but recommend we keep Fallback-Chain as a short encoded string (no spaces) to avoid parsing issues in downstream infra. Also limit chain length to 4.

priya.sundar: For trace UI: show an inline tiny table: step | variant | reason | latency delta. When user clicks a step show full policy inputs. Add a "copy simulation payload" button to help SEs file tickets.

zach.lee: Telemetry: add an alert when fallback_rate for premium tier in any region > 0.5% for 1h, and a secondary alert for repeated fallback spikes tied to policy changes.

maria.gomez: Acceptance criteria (short):
- Headers emitted as spec above for all routed requests.
- Traces auto-sampled when Fallback-Chain present.
- Routing panel in trace UI with timeline + simulate button.
- New metrics exposed and 2 default dashboards (per-tier and per-region).
- Hashing applied to tenant identifiers in public views.

cheng.wu: I'll own the header emit + sampling change (PR incoming).

zach.lee: I'll add the metrics and example Grafana panels.

priya.sundar: I'll mock the routing decision panel and the simulate flow in Figma.

ryan-bot: FYI: ops runbook update required for "fallback surge" — linking page once PR merged.

maria.gomez: Timeline: aim to have staging end-to-end in 2 weeks. If we can instrument forced-sample-on-fallback quickly, that should catch most of the repros.

zach.lee: One last ask — can we include a tiny human-readable reason code (quota/latency/region) in the header so operators don't need to open the trace to triage?

maria.gomez: Yes, include reason=<quota|latency|cap|config> in Fallback-Chain. Keep the string short.

cheng.wu: PR link when ready and I'll review the runtime change for adding headers.

maria.gomez: Perfect. Thanks all — assigning follow-ups in Asana. :thumbsup:
